title: One address change, eight systems
objective: Learners follow one member's address change through eight enterprise systems and see how point-to-point versus event-driven integration decides what the member experiences and whether the data ends up consistent when one system is down.

recommended.why: A narrated story with a character, a conflict and a resolution makes coupling and blast radius memorable for architects and non-architects alike.

alternative.why: A narrated story versus a 3D walkthrough versus the review diagram: which makes coupling and blast radius stick?

assumptions: Systems, timings and names are illustrative; no real health plan, product configuration or SLA is implied
Five systems hold the address: CRM (system of record), master data, claims, billing and analytics
Point-to-point: the CRM calls the four downstream systems synchronously in a fixed order with a 10 s timeout, and rolls back only its own save on failure
Event-driven: the CRM publishes one AddressChanged event; each subscriber updates independently and a retry queue (Platform Event replay in Salesforce terms) redelivers to billing when it returns
Billing is down for about 20 minutes; nobody resends the change by hand in the point-to-point case
Salesforce names map the generic roles; claims and billing stay generic because they are usually not Salesforce, and Apex callouts stand in for the synchronous integration layer
units: response time: seconds the member waits after tapping Save
real time: milliseconds after Save (story playback runs separately, up to 30 s)
integrations: connections to build and run
checkDescription: Event-driven (or no outage): Maria sees "Saved" and all five address holders end on the new address. Point-to-point with the outage: the save fails, the CRM keeps the old address, and the systems out of step are exactly those updated before the billing timeout. Events run in time order and the names switch changes nothing else.
expectAtDefaults: m.style === 'event' && m.outage && m.saveOk && m.consistent && m.events.some(e => e.kind === 'queued')

learnerPrompts.predict: Billing goes down while Maria is saving. Before you play it: with point-to-point calls, which systems will have her new address at the end, and what will she see?
learnerPrompts.explain: Switch between point-to-point and event-driven with the outage on. Why does one failing system decide Maria's experience in one design but not the other, and what did the event-driven design need (the queue) to stay consistent?
